_label: Evidence archive: the registrar's receipts for the studio's domains (2009-2016)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: the registrar's receipts for the studio's domains (2009-2016)

content: A domain registrar's billing record for the studio's account, held as the registrar's own comma-separated export for 2009 together with forty-two PDF invoices, running from 2009-01-04 to 2016-01-05. It shows that on 2009-03-16 at 00:45:06 UTC the account registered the domain WTFISART.COM, on receipt 158832568, for $1.99 plus a $0.20 ICANN fee; that at 01:07:15 UTC the same night it bought 'Economy Classic Hosting Linux' for wtfisart.com at $4.99, on receipt 158833357; and that the hosting was then paid for monthly, at $4.99 with a zero-rated bandwidth line, on 2009-04-15, 2009-05-15, 2009-06-15, 2009-07-25, 2009-08-15, 2009-09-15, 2009-10-15, 2009-11-15 and 2009-12-15. In the same transaction as the domain registration the account also bought an 'Economy Quick Blogcast' for $9.98, which was refunded at 01:20:25 UTC that night on receipt 158832568R, thirty-five minutes after purchase. Separately the account registered GROWINGALOHA.COM on 2009-01-04 and renewed it on 2010-01-05. This is a third party's business record of the studio's account, and it dates the domain and its hosting from fourteen days before the Sotheby's sale of 30 March 2009. The invoices continue past that first year under a second account number, and the paragraphs below set out what they add: the re-registration of WTFISART.COM in 2011, the registration of METACONCEPTUALART.COM in the same order, and renewals running to 2016.

referred_to_by.content: Evidence status: a third party's business record, and the firmest dating evidence in this collection for the website. The registrar generated these receipts, numbered them in its own sequence, and timestamped them in UTC; the studio could not set those dates, and the record can in principle be confirmed by the registrar from its own systems. It is held as the registrar's export, 4,931 bytes, SHA-256 0b4c8f9c660734765666279ff2c5a3f5a3f72219e3e9ff872d6e1e49ba8a1399, and as the matching PDF invoices, of which the three for 2009-03-16 are: the registration and blogcast purchase, 137,163 bytes, SHA-256 0bcec2aef8bd16e3ce2a60d02ab407d1ed76a7a15b86ca0270a1fd0ae6550cb0; its refund, 114,428 bytes, SHA-256 b963cd88dad2d6e5d90db67c55699ebb854e1180eb5d688c4840b9d4aa695d89; and the hosting purchase, 113,079 bytes, SHA-256 7cae6887d52c650ff7ac4998a67cc3b5bb51fcaf9e9266a5a6a97926c3bc772d. The documents themselves are not published: they carry the account holder's postal address, telephone number and mailbox, and the last four digits of a payment card. Checksums are published instead, as with the consignment agreement, so that the held files can later be shown unaltered without being disclosed. The size and SHA-256 of all forty-two invoices are published as a manifest beside this record, at data/evidence/registrar-receipts/manifest.json.

What this establishes, and it is narrow. The domain wtfisart.com was registered, and hosting for it was bought, on 2009-03-16, fourteen days before the auction of 30 March 2009 at which the studio consigned lot 16; and hosting on that account went on being paid for every month until at least 2009-12-15. Until now the date on which the studio first took the domain was undetermined from any public source, and the collection said so. It is now fixed by a document the studio did not write. Two qualifications belong with it. Only the first hosting purchase names wtfisart.com; the nine renewals name the product alone, so that they are renewals of that same account is an inference from the record's shape, reasonable but not stated in it. And one payment falls out of the monthly pattern, on 2009-07-25 rather than the fifteenth.

What it does not establish. It says nothing whatever about what was served at the domain. A registration is a name; hosting is rented space; neither is a published page, and no capture of the domain exists from that period. The WTFIA folder of source documents, worked on until the week before the sale, is what the studio assembled for the site, and the reconstruction record sets out that no HTML from the 2009 site survives anywhere. So the position is now: the domain and the hosting are documented from 2009-03-16, and what if anything stood at that address in 2009 remains unevidenced. This record also says nothing about the auction designation, and nothing about the 2007 origin asserted elsewhere in this collection.

The lapse, the parked page of 2011, and the re-registration that followed it. No renewal of WTFISART.COM appears among the invoices of the first year, which run to 2010-01-05 and do contain a renewal of the other domain. A registration taken on 2009-03-16 for one year would fall due on 2010-03-16. The Internet Archive's earliest capture of the domain, on 2011-02-10, shows a parked advertising page carrying no studio content, which is what a registrar commonly serves at an address whose registration has lapsed. That capture is therefore evidence about February 2011 and not about 2009, and the records of this collection which read it as positive evidence that the site was not live in 2009 have been narrowed to say what it can carry. The fuller set of invoices adds that the lapse was not permanent: on 2011-10-16, eight months after that capture, the account registered WTFISART.COM again, on receipt 367713033, in a bulk order of six .COM names at $9.59 each. An earlier version of this record said that no renewal of the domain appeared anywhere in it. That was true of the first year's invoices, which were all this record then held, and it is not true of the whole run.

The blogcast, bought and refunded in thirty-five minutes. In the same transaction as the domain registration, at 00:45:06 UTC on 2009-03-16, the account bought a registrar-hosted blogging product, 'Economy Quick Blogcast', for $9.98, and at 01:20:25 UTC it was refunded in full. The studio recalled an early blog of about this period which it has been unable to find. This purchase accounts for the recollection and, equally, explains why nothing has been found: the product was returned the same night, and nothing in this collection evidences a blog published at that time. The studio's only blog located on any platform is one opened in November 2014, whose owning profile records its own creation in that month.

The other domain, and a correction that is itself withdrawn. The same account registered GROWINGALOHA.COM on 2009-01-04, on receipt 146295715, and renewed it on 2010-01-05, on receipt 213590943. That is the sibling site whose Dreamweaver template and stylesheet the reconstruction copies, and those two purchases are documented by the registrar's own invoices. The public registry disagrees, and the paragraph below sets out why the invoices are the better evidence. This record previously carried a correction stating that the receipts do not name Sun and Rain Works, that the billing name on every line is the studio principal's own, and that the business is named nowhere in them. That correction was wrong and is withdrawn. It was drawn from the registrar's comma-separated export, which has no billing-name column at all, so the absence of a field was taken for the absence of a fact. The PDF invoices carry a 'Bill To' block, and on every one of the forty-two examined it gives the account holder's name, a postal address, and the line 'Sun and Rain Works'. That includes receipt 158832568, the registration of WTFISART.COM itself, and receipt 146295715, the registration of GROWINGALOHA.COM. The business is named by the registrar, in the registrar's own business records, on the first invoice of the run and on the last.

The name as the registrar recorded it. Receipt 158832568 records the string WTFISART.COM. A domain name carries no spaces and no punctuation, so the string does not settle how it is to be read: it reads as a question, 'WTF is art?', and equally as a statement, 'WTF is art', or 'WTF Is Art' taken as a title. Both readings are present in the string as the registrar printed it at 00:45:06 UTC on 2009-03-16; neither is supplied after the fact. The 'Bill To' block of the same invoice names Sun and Rain Works, so the name was taken by the business under which the studio works.

The studio's reading of the registration, given in 2026. The studio holds that the double reading was deliberate: that by choosing a name which is at once a question and a declaration it named the work and declared it art, and that the registration under the business's name puts that declaration on record. That is the studio's account of its intent, and this record keeps it apart from what the receipt shows. A registrar prints whatever string is bought, so the receipt fixes the date of the name and the business that took it, and records nothing of why the name was chosen. Nor does the business name mark this purchase out: the same 'Bill To' line appears on all forty-two invoices, including the registration of GROWINGALOHA.COM and names unrelated to this collection. What the receipt adds to the studio's account is independent dating. The words the studio now reads as the work's declaration were taken by the studio on 2009-03-16, fourteen days before the sale, on a document the studio did not write.

What the later invoices add, 2011 to 2016. Thirty of the forty-two invoices post-date the first year and fall under a second account number, the account having been renumbered between 2010 and 2011; the billing address moves from Hawai'i to Eugene, Oregon across the same gap. Three registrations among them bear on this collection. On 2011-10-16, on receipt 367713033, the account registered six .COM names in one bulk order at $9.59 each, among them WTFISART.COM, SUNANDRAINWORKS.COM and METACONCEPTUALART.COM, with privacy added to those and to others three days later on receipt 368276263. That is the earliest date this collection can place on METACONCEPTUALART.COM, which is the domain at which it is itself published. SUNANDRAINWORKS.ORG and SUNANDRAINWORKS.INFO follow on 2011-12-23, on receipt 385638142. ARTMARKETREFORM.ORG follows on 2012-11-21, on receipt 484082135, a year before the archived captures of art-market-reform material that the archived-websites record describes, with .NET and .INFO and four ARTMARKETBUBBLE names on 2013-05-23. Renewals run through the set: WTFISART.COM on 2012-10-17, 2015-01-04 and 2016-01-04; SUNANDRAINWORKS.ORG on 2013-01-05, 2014-12-22 and 2015-12-28; ARTMARKETREFORM.ORG on 2014-11-22 and 2015-11-23. The run ends at 2016-01-05, which is where the studio's held invoices stop rather than necessarily where the account's activity stops. Receipt 634164015 of 2013-12-27 also carries 'Domain Backorder' lines at $20.98 each against WTFISART.COM, SUNANDRAINWORKS.COM, WEGOTSOLDOUT.COM, WHATHEDGEFUNDS.COM and ARTMARKETREFORM.ORG, bundled with auction-membership renewals. A backorder is ordinarily a bid to capture a name when its current registration lapses, and these are names the account already held; what those lines mean on this account is not determined here. The same invoices register a number of further names unrelated to this collection, which are not itemised here.

The public registry contradicts these invoices, and the invoices are the better evidence. The domain registry was queried by RDAP on 2026-09-12, and it gives creation dates that do not match the studio's documents: SUNANDRAINWORKS.COM 2023-01-06, METACONCEPTUALART.COM 2023-01-27, WTFISART.COM 2024-08-29, and GROWINGALOHA.COM 2011-10-04. The invoices date the first three to a single bulk order of 2011-10-16 and the fourth to 2009-01-04. All four discrepancies run the same way, and the explanation is the one the wtfisart.com record already sets out for that domain: a registry creation date describes the registration object that currently exists, not the first time a registrant took the name. When a registration lapses the object is destroyed, and a later registration of the same string is a new object with a new date and a new handle. The original date is not retained anywhere in the public record and cannot be recovered from it. So a reader checking WHOIS today would conclude that the studio's own domain, and the domain at which this collection is published, are both two years old. They are not, and these invoices are what shows it. The consequence for anyone weighing this collection is worth stating in the open: on the question of when the studio first held these names, a dated invoice from the vendor is a business record and a registry creation date is not evidence at all, because the registry has no memory of what it has deleted. The consequence for the studio is less comfortable. Four registrations are now evidenced by held documents and by nothing else, so if the PDFs were lost there is no public source that would replace them. That is why the size and SHA-256 of all forty-two are published in the manifest beside this record, and why the originals should be preserved somewhere other than one machine.
